title: EvalSift – 100 hand-labeled LLM agent traces
author: Eddie-Town

excerpt: Find out how your LLM agent actually fails before you write a single eval. EvalSift Lite is a free, MIT-licensed Python tool (3.10+, no dependencies, no API key) for error analysis on LLM agent traces: it validates a traces.jsonl file, grades each trace with deterministic code checks, and writes a Markdown/HTML report of what failed. It comes with a case study: 100 traces from a tool-using support agent, labeled by hand. Get the full Solo kit (100 labeled traces + data): git clone <repo-url> && cd evalsift-lite python -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate pip install -e . python -m evalsift_lite.demo # writes report.html, report.md, results.jsonl The demo grades 8 traces from a fake support agent with 4 planted failures and catches all 4. A support agent for a fictional outdoor store, with order, stock and policy tools. One labeler, 88 pass and 12 fail. Full breakdown: case-study/FAILURES.md Examples worth reading: - q087: "free over $75" is not "free at $75" - q016: asking instead of looking - q046: a correct answer to the wrong question - q086: off by one day The 100 questions are in case-study/questions.jsonl, so you can run them on your own agent and see whether it makes the same mistakes. One JSON object per line: trace_id, input, output, optional steps[] (each with type set to llm or tool, plus name, args, result, error) and optional metadata{}. Then: python -m evalsift_lite.demo --traces your_traces.jsonl --out-dir out/ This runs the built-in checks; add your own in evalsift_lite/graders.py. EvalSift adds agent skills for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor that walk you through error analysis, building a failure taxonomy, writing an LLM judge, checking that judge against human labels, and gating regressions in CI. It also includes the full case-study data: all 100 traces, the labels with notes, and a note on how the labels were made. MIT. See LICENSE.
